Error Behaviors

Error Behaviors provide a deterministic, centralized mechanism for handling failures that occur during pipeline execution. Error behaviors normalize, finalize, and expose error conditions as a canonical VaultErrorShape, ensuring that all failures are handled consistently regardless of where they originate.

Error Contract Summary

  • Error behaviors must not throw or rethrow errors
  • All errors are normalized into a canonical VaultErrorShape
  • Error behaviors must not mutate state snapshots
  • Error behaviors do not emit successful state snapshots
  • Core error handling is always executed and cannot be omitted

The Error contract guarantees that error handling is deterministic and isolated. If any pipeline stage throws or rejects, pipeline execution is immediately terminated and control is transferred to the Error stage. The in-flight candidate value is discarded, no reducers are executed, and no successful snapshot is emitted. This ensures that failures never result in partially applied state or ambiguous pipeline outcomes.

Error behaviors do not participate in value derivation, scheduling, or pipeline control. Their sole responsibility is to provide a compatibility and observation surface for already-finalized error conditions.

Error Stage

The Error Stage runs whenever any earlier pipeline stage throws or rejects. It serves as the exclusive execution boundary for error handling and guarantees that all failures are converted into a canonical VaultErrorShape before state is finalized.

When entered, the Error Stage terminates the current pipeline execution and prevents further processing of the candidate value. No reducers, taps, or persistence stages are executed.

Error behaviors:

  • Receive the raw thrown or rejected value
  • Operate exclusively on a normalized VaultErrorShape
  • Have read-only access to the immutable state snapshot
  • May inspect, classify, or enrich error metadata
  • Must preserve error pipeline integrity

Core Pipeline Stage

The Error stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle. A core error behavior is executed first to guarantee error normalization into a canonical VaultError. This behavior cannot be omitted. Additional error behaviors may be layered after the core behavior and are optional.

Error behaviors do not resume pipeline execution and do not suppress error finalization. Their responsibility ends once the error state has been committed and exposed.

Add-on Error Callback Behaviors

In addition to core error normalization and transformation, FeatureCells may opt into add-on error callback behaviors. These behaviors observe the finalized VaultErrorShape after it has been committed to state and may perform supplemental, observational handling such as logging, diagnostics, or compatibility callbacks. Error callbacks do not replace, suppress, or alter error finalization.

Legacy error callbacks exist solely for convenience and backward compatibility. The primary mechanism for observing and responding to errors is the reactive vault.state().error. Callback-based handling should not be relied upon for core application logic.

Fluent Errors() API

A FeatureCell may declare multiple error callbacks using the fluent .errors() API. This API accepts an ordered array of error callbacks that are executed sequentially after the error state has been finalized. Callback registration occurs during FeatureCell initialization.

Error callbacks are strictly observational. They do not influence pipeline control flow, do not transform the error, and always return VAULT_NOOP.

An empty errors array is ignored and has no effect on pipeline execution.

Engineer-Supplied Error Callbacks

Error callbacks are supplied by engineers during FeatureCell initialization and execute exclusively after the authoritative error state has been committed. Each callback receives the normalized VaultErrorShape and an immutable state snapshot. Callbacks must not throw, must not mutate state, and must not attempt to resume pipeline execution.

Note

Although multiple error callbacks may be composed, callback logic should remain narrowly scoped and observational. Complex or interdependent callbacks can obscure intent and complicate failure analysis. Error callbacks are most effective when limited to logging, diagnostics, or transitional compatibility concerns.

Add-on Error Transform Behaviors

In addition to core error normalization, FeatureCells may opt into add-on error transform behaviors. These behaviors participate directly in the Error Stage and are permitted to transform the current VaultErrorShape before it is committed and exposed.

Error transform behaviors execute after core error normalization and before error callbacks. Each transform receives the raw thrown error, the current VaultErrorShape, and an immutable state snapshot. Based on this input, a transform may return a new VaultErrorShape or VAULT_NOOP to preserve the existing value.

Unlike callbacks, error transform behaviors are authoritative. When a transform returns a new VaultErrorShape, that value becomes the active error for all subsequent transforms and for final error state commitment.

Error transform behaviors must not throw, must not mutate state, and must not attempt to resume or suppress error finalization. Any exceptions raised by a transform are isolated, logged, and do not interrupt downstream error handling.

Note

Multiple error transform behaviors may be composed. When configured, they execute sequentially in the exact order they are declared in the FeatureCell definition. Each transform receives the current VaultErrorShape produced by the preceding behavior—starting with core error normalization—and may replace it or pass it through unchanged.

Because transforms are applied cumulatively, their order is semantically significant. Error transform behaviors should remain narrowly scoped and intentional. Overlapping or order-dependent transforms can obscure error provenance and complicate failure analysis.

Global Error Service

After error normalization, transformation, and callback handling have completed, the finalized VaultErrorShape is published to the Global Error Service. This service provides a centralized, observable view of the most recent Vault error across all FeatureCells.

The Global Error Service does not participate in pipeline execution, error transformation, or control flow. It exists solely as an application-level coordination surface for errors that have already been fully processed and committed by the Vault.

Subscription to the Global Error Service is opt-in and requires explicit consumer code to instantiate the VaultErrorService singleton and subscribe to its observable interface. Errors are emitted regardless of whether any consumer is listening, ensuring that pipeline behavior remains deterministic and unaffected by global observers.

The Global Error Service represents the final stage of the Vault error lifecycle. Once an error is published globally, no further pipeline activity occurs for the failed update.
